method: Manual source-sufficiency review by the implementing assistant. No LLM judge and no frozen evaluator score.

rubric.sufficient: Visible public sources directly support a complete answer without guesswork.
rubric.partial: Visible sources support an important part of the answer but omit a requested condition, distinction, or stopping rule.
rubric.miss: Visible sources do not support the requested answer, despite the contract being documented elsewhere in the repository.

cases.rationale: Direct omission-contract source says honor omitted_counts, omission is non-critical, and truncation does not certify completeness.
Visible response-contract source identifies omitted_counts as the bounded field to inspect for omissions; extra sources are noisy but non-blocking.
Visible omission contract explicitly separates truncated from insufficient_evidence.
Returned source only lists status/kind semantics and does not say truncation omits only non-critical material; the needed sentence exists in docs/mcp-response-contract.md but was not surfaced.
Direct source explains the role of omitted_counts and its relation to truncated responses.
Direct source distinguishes top-level omitted_counts from documentation_gap.bounds.omitted_counts.
Visible source tells the client to honor omitted_counts, but the requested complete companion field list kind/sources/missing is not surfaced.
Direct source explains that truncated omission is non-critical but does not certify complete project-context coverage.
Returned product-evaluation text is unrelated; the documented safe distinction between insufficient_evidence and ordinary truncation is missed.
Direct authoring-handoff source names documentation_gap.bounds.omitted_counts.
Direct maintained-doc authority rule says present behavior uses maintained source-of-truth documentation as primary.
Direct source names releases, changes, migration, deprecation, and compatibility history as CHANGELOG-primary cases.
Direct source says CHANGELOG must not outrank current source-of-truth for present-state questions.
Migration is explicitly listed as a history case where CHANGELOG is primary.
Direct present-state caveat answers that a matching CHANGELOG entry is not enough to outrank maintained current docs.
Returned API-key and registry material is unrelated; the current-vs-history authority rule exists in searchable project docs but is not retrieved.
Direct source says change/release-history questions use CHANGELOG as primary.
Direct source says current contracts use maintained source-of-truth documentation.
Direct source says CHANGELOG may supplement but must not outrank current source-of-truth.
Visible authority rule supports the supplement-vs-replace distinction.
Retrieval confuses splitting a comparison request with indexing/chunk splitting; the no-pre-split policy exists in SKILL.md and the installed agent workflow resource.
Direct workflow sources say lookup_queries are narrow same-question recall help for translation/facet decomposition, not a batch channel.
Direct Gap-directed follow-up source says split only after the first packet leaves a concrete independently answerable requested part missing.
Returned exact-version sources are unrelated; the known-source policy says to use an issued bounded source read.

Visible docs_context contract says the host may answer covered claims without claiming completeness, but it does not surface the explicit stop rule: stop on sufficient visible evidence even when context_quality is unverified, or on no progress.
Public result is insufficient_evidence with no source, although the stop rule is explicitly documented in SKILL.md and the installed workflow resource.
Visible sources do not contain the documented at-most-one non-automatic rephrase_question rule.
Direct workflow sources say follow the exact typed recommended_next_action, obtain confirmation when needed, then retry the original question unchanged after success.
Returned benchmark comparison is unrelated; the maintained workflow instead prescribes targeted same-need recovery within existing limits rather than global budget/top-k expansion.
Returned query configuration and test-policy material is unrelated; SKILL.md explicitly says same need/different vocabulary should use narrow lookup_queries.

observations: query_coverage is not semantic answer sufficiency: F21 and F24 report full query coverage while their visible evidence is off-topic.
context_quality partial/unverified does not imply the answer is unusable: several sufficient cases expose the correct direct source despite conservative quality metadata.
The V13 omission family generalizes reasonably well, but negated/safety paraphrases F04 and F09 still miss an existing response-contract paragraph.
Current-vs-history authority generalizes strongly: 9/10 fresh prompts are sufficient; F16 is the main paraphrase miss.
Workflow/recovery policy is the weak area: only 3/10 fresh prompts are fully sufficient, with failures dominated by semantic ambiguity and vocabulary mismatch rather than missing documentation.
